Alice M.: Quick proposal — let's try a kernel-aware 'batched token slate' policy that maps max_tokens_per_batch to kernel-fit and KV-frag signals per accelerator (A10 / T4 / L4 / A100 / H100). Goal: reduce tail latency regressions from bad kernel choices while keeping cost-efficient batching.

Ben K.: Can you paste the heuristics and a short perf summary? want numbers to show to infra folks :eyes:

Ciara: TL;DR from the last profiling sweep (attached flamegraphs + pprof links):
```
profiling summary (canary run 2755550000 -> 2755553000):
- H100: prefer kernel nvfused_v3 for seq>=2048, safe max_tokens_per_batch ~= 128k, tail p95 reg ~+2% vs baseline
- A100: nvfused_v2 best for mixed seqs, safe ~= 96k tokens, observed p95 +5% when kv_frag > 30%
- A10: mixed kernel; fallback to int8-kern for >64k tokens, recommend cap 64k nominal, 48k when kv_frag > 25%
- L4: best-effort kernel, cap 32k (kv frag causes larger tail effects)
- T4: memory-limited, cap 16k, prefer small-request packing
```
Snippet for policy (proto-ish):
```
policy {
  if accelerator == H100 and kernel_fit == HIGH -> max_tokens_per_batch = 128000
  if accelerator == A100 and kv_frag < 0.25 -> max_tokens_per_batch = 96000
  if accelerator == A10 and kv_frag >= 0.25 -> max_tokens_per_batch = 48000
  if accelerator in [L4] -> max_tokens_per_batch = 32000
  if accelerator in [T4] -> max_tokens_per_batch = 16000
  if tail_regression > 0.12 -> revert_kernel = previous_stable
}
```
Links: pprof: https://perf.redwood.local/pprof/2755550000, flame: https://perf.redwood.local/flame/2755550000

Dan: FYI — in the canary we saw a regression on A100 for stream-regen workload: p95 +18% when we forced nvfused_v2 with large batch tokens. I think the kv-frag threshold logic needs to be stricter for A100 to avoid that. Suggest auto-revert threshold of +12% p95 and an immediate routing to smaller max_tokens for that cardset.

Eva: Agree. Also propose queue policy tweak: when KV cache hit ratio < 0.6, bias the batcher to form smaller slates (prefer fewer requests per aggregate) so KV frag doesn't explode. Pseudo-rule: if kv_hit < 0.6 -> target_tokens_per_batch *= 0.6 and set max_batch_wait_ms = 10.

Ben K.: Sounds reasonable. Can we add a small experiment matrix? quick A/B: keep current baseline, rollout policy, and aggressive-policy with auto-revert. Want metrics: p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, kv-frag%.

Ciara: Yep — experiment plan drafted: 2 week canary across these cardsets, sample workloads: chat-streaming (short), long-context generation (seq>=2048), embeddings-hot (many small reqs). Metrics -> [p50,p95,p99, tail_regression, tokens-per-second, cost/tok]. I'll attach runbook after i finish the notebook.

perf-bot: benchmark summary (automated): canary-2755550000 -> baseline diff: A100 p95 +6.4%, H100 p95 +1.9%, A10 p95 +3.2% when kv_frag>0.25 :eyes:

Dan: If perf-bot numbers hold, let's tighten A100 condition: require kv_frag<0.2 to allow >80k tokens.

Alice M.: Plan: I'll land policy PR with conservative caps from Ciara and Eva's queue tweak. We will gate rollout behind the experiment and auto-revert on >12% p95 regression. Thanks all — please react when you've read :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch/batched-token-slate -> canary (2 nodes per cardset) at 2755554400

Ben K.: ack

Eva: ack :thumbsup:

Ciara: putting runbook in the canary folder now and will tag the SRE on-call.

Alice M.: closing loop — will post results in ~48h.
